name: Photosynthesis Rate Calculator
seoDesc: Photosynthesis rate is the carbon fixed per unit leaf area per unit time. Free photosynthesis rate calculator: enter your values and get carbon fixed, rate, d
summary:
Photosynthesis rate is the carbon fixed per unit leaf area per unit time. It returns carbon fixed, rate, daily carbon gain at this rate and dry matter equivalent per day, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator converts between the ways it is reported — µmol CO₂ per m² per second, mg CO₂ per dm² per hour and grams of dry matter — so measurements from a gas analyser can be compared with growth data. Every result is derived from the boxes you fill in, so changing one input updates the whole panel at once. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: How do I use the Photosynthesis Rate?
sections.html:
The form asks only for what the formula needs — nothing is optional decoration.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: net assimilation rate of 12 µmol CO₂/m²/s, leaf area of 0.02 m², measurement period of 10 min.

Substituting them into the formula gives carbon fixed of 144 µmol CO₂, rate of 19.01 mg CO₂/dm²/h, daily carbon gain at this rate of 0.1493 g C/m²/day, dry matter equivalent per day of 0.3285 g/m²/day.

The arithmetic is the page's own: change one box and the result moves by the amount the formula implies, which is the quickest way to convince yourself the tool is honest.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• Net assimilation is photosynthesis minus leaf respiration; gross photosynthesis is higher, and the difference is largest in shade leaves.

  • The 1.584 factor converts µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹ to mg CO₂ dm⁻² h⁻¹ and is worth remembering — it is 44 ÷ 1 000 × 36.

  • Extrapolating a leaf-level rate to a canopy overstates it, because lower leaves are shaded and older.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is simple; the inputs are where things go wrong. The usual culprits:

  • Comparing a net rate with a gross rate.
  • Extrapolating a mid-morning measurement across a whole day.
  • Using leaf area measured flat when the leaf was held at an angle.

faq.q: What is a typical photosynthesis rate?
faq.a: 10–25 µmol CO₂/m²/s for healthy C3 crop leaves in full sun; C4 grasses can exceed 40.

faq.q: Why is the rate lower at midday?
faq.a: Stomatal closure under high vapour pressure deficit and photorespiration both reduce it.

faq.q: What does the Photosynthesis Rate actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns carbon fixed, rate, daily carbon gain at this rate and dry matter equivalent per day. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
